readerContract.humanQuestion: Claude Opus 5.5 changed prices and usage limits. Which change applies to my subscription, and which applies only to API use?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Separate developer token billing from subscription usage limits and understand why the announcement does not prove model-selector access for every individual plan.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No knowledge of APIs, tokens, rate limits or Claude plan names assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: One announcement can change two different meters: API customers pay for tokens used, while subscribers encounter plan usage limits. Neither statement alone proves what one account can select today.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A Claude subscriber sees $4 and $20 prices beside Pro and Max limit changes and wonders whether her monthly bill or model access changed.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A narrow Daily product brief on Anthropic’s September 22 Opus 5.5 availability, API prices and subscription-limit announcement.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can tell which number belongs to developer billing, which change belongs to subscriptions, and what I still need to verify in my own plan.

candidateRepairPreflight.billing: The $4 input and $20 output figures are API prices per million tokens, not monthly subscription prices.
candidateRepairPreflight.limits: Anthropic names Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise for higher five-hour limits but does not quantify the new limits.
candidateRepairPreflight.access: The announcement says all platforms but does not map model-selector eligibility plan by plan; no universal ordinary-chat access claim.
candidateRepairPreflight.claims: Performance, speed, safety and cost-per-task comparisons remain attributed provider claims.
candidateRepairPreflight.distinctness: This is Anthropic plan/API interpretation, not another GPT-6 Sol/Luna availability story.

draftArchitecture.openingJob: Lead with the higher five-hour limits and saveable reset for named Claude subscriptions, then distinguish the secondary developer API prices.
causalSequence: Anthropic announced Opus 5.5 on September 22 and says five-hour limits increased on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans.
Subscription users also receive a rate-limit reset that can be saved for later.
The announcement does not quantify the new limits or map model-selector eligibility for every individual plan.
Developers using the API are billed by token; Anthropic published $4 input and $20 output prices per million tokens.
A reader must check the current selector and plan page for her account while keeping provider performance claims attributed.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A Pro subscriber does not multiply her chat by the $4 API input price. She looks at the subscription plan’s current usage and model access. A developer making API calls uses the token price table instead.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: When another model release mixes a monthly plan name with a per-token table, identify the product surface and meter before comparing costs.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Before treating the announcement as a price change for you, identify whether you use Claude chat, Claude Code or the API, then check the current plan page or model selector for that exact surface.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; The Cocktail Party Explanation; Class Notes; Sources.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No benchmark roundup, universal selector promise, savings claim, invented limit quantity or forced workplace advice.

humourPlan.noneReason: The two-meter distinction is clearer without a decorative comparison.

draftArchitecture.presentationPlan: Use the independently admitted people-free desk illustration: chat and hourglass for the subscription time window, and abstract processed blocks with a counter and receipt for direct API metering. No logos, prices, quantified limits or universal-access symbols.
draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Anthropic says it increased five-hour limits on named paid subscriptions and added a saveable reset, but did not quantify each plan’s new limit. The $4 and $20 figures are separate developer API token prices.
